  • US 10Y T-NOTE: 4.4977 (+0.024)

Today, the US treasury will auction off $39B of 10 year notes at 1 PM after an average distribution of 3 year notes yesterday. The treasury will complete the coupon auctions tomorrow with the 30 year bond ($22B).

Treasury auctions provide key insight into investor appetite for duration amid softening yields and shifting expectations around Federal Reserve policy. The focus will be on demand metrics such as bid-to-cover ratios and foreign participation, particularly as the longer-dated paper often reveals sentiment around inflation and growth prospects. There may be a redirection of foreign funds as a result of auctions as well. The 10 year is a key issue and proxy, as it is an influence on corporate borrowing as well as consumers with mortgages, car loans and other consumer credit loans hinging on that rate.

item.title: Trump: Our deal with China is done, relationship is excellent
item.description:
Trump is out with a message on Truth Social about the deal with China.

Naturally, he wrote it in all caps:

OUR DEAL WITH CHINA IS DONE, SUBJECT TO FINAL APPROVAL WITH PRESIDENT XI AND ME. FULL MAGNETS, AND ANY NECESSARY RARE EARTHS, WILL BE SUPPLIED, UP FRONT, BY CHINA. LIKEWISE, WE WILL PROVIDE TO CHINA WHAT WAS AGREED TO, INCLUDING CHINESE STUDENTS USING OUR COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES (WHICH HAS ALWAYS BEEN GOOD WITH ME!). WE ARE GETTING A TOTAL OF 55% TARIFFS, CHINA IS GETTING 10%. RELATIONSHIP IS EXCELLENT! THANK YOU FOR YOUR ATTENTION TO THIS MATTER!

I guess this is the framework to a deal or whatever. I'm not sure how this took 20 hours of negotiating to get but I'm sure there are some other things moving behind the scenes. Note that Trump says "we will provide to China what has been agreed to" without elaborating aside from students.

Futures are bouncing around on this but unmoved from before he sent out the message. Part of that is confusion about what he's talking about and the tariff rates, as the US rate was lowered to 30% last month. Maybe the Chinese side or a leak will offer some proper context.

This article was written by Adam Button at www.forexlive.com.

Central banks bought a record 1,000 metric tons of gold last year—twice the decade average—making gold the second-most held reserve asset after the U.S. dollar.
Gold now accounts for 20% of total reserves, boosted by both buying and rising prices. Meanwhile, the dollar’s share fell to 46%, partly due to sanctions on Russia that froze $300 billion in assets, raising concerns about dollar dependence.
Central banks are also turning to other currencies like the Canadian and Australian dollars. The euro remains stable at around 16% but could gain from growing global unease over U.S. deficits and trade policy.

item.title: A New Chapter for Money: Blending Crypto and Traditional Systems
item.description:
Consider moving money around the world in seconds or buying a stake in a building by simply holding a digital token. These concepts would have appeared unthinkable a few years ago. However, in 2025, users and institutions understand how blockchain and cryptocurrencies help address typical financial problems. That’s why, in 2025, Institutional adoption has accelerated dramatically, with Bitcoin ETFs attracting over $55 billion in projected inflows.

Traditional finance has served us well for decades, but it can be time-consuming, complex, and costly. Sometimes there are delays in transactions, and high fees for various services (e.g., maintenance, overdrafts, wire transfers).

Many places still lack dependable financial infrastructure, excluding individuals from the global economy. These issues pave the way for a new approach—one that incorporates digital tools where they are most useful while preserving what is currently effective.

This article explores why old traditional systems are struggling to meet current demand, and how crypto & blockchain help overcome those problems.

Why Old Systems Struggle

Some of the major challenges with traditional banking are:

● Slow Settlements: Cross-border transfers might take several days to complete, resulting in delays and additional fees.

● Opaque Procedures: Fees and currency rates are not always disclosed. You may not know precisely how much you are paying until the transfer is completed.

● Limited Access: People in locations with limited bank branches or insecure internet cannot readily manage or transfer their money.

Collectively, these gaps demonstrate why a new viewpoint is required. Instead of knocking down trustworthy banks, entrepreneurs are working to improve them by incorporating blockchain capabilities.

How Crypto Helps Overcome These Issues

Blockchain technology provides characteristics that directly solve these problem points:

● Real-time settlements allow transactions to clear in minutes, decreasing uncertainty for both senders and recipients.

● Transparent ledgers record all transactions on a public or permissioned chain. Users may track payments and fees in real time, revealing hidden expenditures.

● Tokenized Assets: Physical assets, like as real estate, art, or commodities, may be converted into digital tokens. This allows investors to purchase fewer shares without having to complete onerous paperwork.

By integrating these benefits with current banking methods, we gain both speed and security. Instead of perceiving cryptocurrency and banks as competitors, they may collaborate to make finance more efficient and inclusive.

A Practical Example: Tokenized Real Estate

Consider someone looking to invest in a rental property in another nation. In the past, they may have faced costly entrance fees, extensive legal paperwork, and the necessity for local property management. Today, a real estate company may "tokenize" a building by issuing digital shares over a secure network. Now:

● An investor can acquire a few tokens that represent a portion of the property.

● Smart contracts can automate rent payments to token holders.

● All ownership records and transactions are kept on a public ledger.

This strategy makes the market more accessible to smaller investors while also speeding up the process. It also cuts expenses by eliminating certain intermediaries and bureaucracy.

As a consequence, more individuals may engage without having to go through complex legal procedures or pay big upfront fees.

Bringing It All Together with Real-World Innovation

A typical case study of a corporation that combines the old with the modern is MultiBank. It is rooted in conventional finance, with over 15 global licenses and a solid experience in FX and derivatives and has created a regulated environment for digital asset innovation.

The platform, like similar corporations, demonstrates how businesses may bridge the gap between compliance, risk management, and safe custody solutions in blockchain initiatives. Instead of abstract roadmaps and hoopla, they prioritize tangible collaborations.

For example, a $3 billion real estate tokenization agreement between MAG and Mavryk highlights how Web3 can increase liquidity and worldwide involvement. Physical assets are digitized and exchanged on a safe, regulated platform that appeals to both crypto-native users and traditional investors.

Moving Forward: What You Can Do Today

If you're intrigued about how cryptocurrency may simplify your financial life, take simple steps:

● Explore Educational Resources

Look for concise guides to blockchain basics and how it relates to traditional finance.

Many articles and videos explain these principles in common terms, avoiding jargon.

● Try a tokenized investment

Some platforms provide low-cost entry points, such as digital shares of real estate or art.

You may test the waters by purchasing a modest amount to see how the procedure feels before committing to a significant number.

● Ask questions

Contact your bank or financial advisor and inquire about regulated cryptocurrency services. Institutions that support blockchain frequently provide a smoother onboarding experience for new customers and are willing to explain costs, settlement timeframes, and security precautions.

Learning about tokenized assets or trying with a basic blockchain transfer will allow you to observe firsthand how crypto is not replacing, but rather reinventing, traditional finance.

The future of finance depends on both innovation and trust functioning together.

This article was written by FL Contributors at www.forexlive.com.

item.title: ECB's Kazaks: Keeping 2% inflation will require some further cuts for fine tuning
item.description:
• Quite likely keeping 2% inflation will require some further cuts for fine tuning.
  • Market pricing of one more cut or so not out of the realm of the baseline.
  • Fine-tuning cuts will very much depend on how the economy develops.
  • May at some point, not yet by any means, go into accommodative territory.
  • Must be cautious about potential persistence of undershooting.
  • We need to take care of those risks of a too persistent or large deviation from target.
  • So far, seems deflationary effect of trade tensions could dominate, but final outcome open.
  • June cut to ensure that inflation in 2026 eventually turns the corner and starts returning towards 2%.

The ECB continues to look very confident that the risk ahead is undershooting on their 2% target and assigns very little risk to renewed inflationary pressures. Hope for them that they are right.

item.title: USDJPY Technical Analysis – All eyes on the US CPI
item.description:
Fundamental Overview

The USD remains mostly rangebound even though the better than expected NFP report triggered a slightly more hawkish repricing in interest rates expectations and sent Treasury yields higher.

The next two key events for the greenback are the US CPI today and the FOMC decision next week. The dollar will need hawkish stuff to get a boost.

On the JPY side, the currency remains weak almost across the board as the BoJ is said to reduce its bond buying tapering plan and we continue to hear from officials that a change in rates is not going to happen anytime soon. The central bank continues to wait for US-Japan trade deal and the evolution of inflation.

USDJPY Technical Analysis – Daily Timeframe

On the daily chart, we can see that USDJPY is consolidating between the 142.35 and 146.00 levels. We’ve been ranging for quite some time as the market continues to wait for stronger signals to pick a direction. For now, the target for the buyers remains the 148.32 resistance, while the sellers will look for a break below the 142.35 support to extend the drop into the 140.00 handle next.

USDJPY Technical Analysis – 4 hour Timeframe

On the 4 hour chart, we can see that we have a support zone around the 144.32 level. This is where we can expect the buyers to keep stepping in with a defined risk below the support and target the 146.28 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to pile in for a drop back into the 142.35 support.

USDJPY Technical Analysis – 1 hour Timeframe

On the 1 hour chart, we can see that we have a minor upward trendline defining the bullish momentum on this timeframe. The buyers will likely continue to lean on the trendline to keep pushing into new highs, while the sellers will look for a break below the trendline and the support to target the 142.35 level next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

Upcoming Catalysts

Today, we have the US CPI. Tomorrow, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures and US PPI. On Friday, we conclude the week with the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment report.

item.title: EU aims for US trade talks to extend past Trump’s July deadline.
item.description:
Seems like talks are not proceeding that quickly despite Trump saying that his previous 50% tariff threat sped up the process. The US-China talks are a testament to that as they haven't reached a deal but just a framework to implement the Geneva agreements.

Of course, this shouldn't be a surprise given that this stuff takes a lot of time. The important thing is that tariffs were brought down to the 10% level and businesses continue to report that they are planning with the 10-20% tariff range in mind.

Therefore, we might just keep on kicking the can down the road with new 90-days pauses but what matters is that the baseline remains 10%.

item.title: What are the main events for today?
item.description:
In the European session, we don't have anything on the agenda except a few ECB speakers. In the American session, all eyes will be on the US CPI report.

The Core CPI Y/Y is expected at 2.9% vs 2.8% prior, while the M/M figure is seen at 0.3% vs 0.2% prior. Inflation is expected to pick up a bit due to tariffs but the Fed has stated that it's willing to look through tariff related hikes if the uncertainty on the trade side eases.

The central bank expects to be able to cut in the latter part of this year but it's still unclear if it's going to be two cuts or just one. It will certainly be hard for them to deliver rate cuts if the economic data remains strong and the disinflationary trend stalls or even reverses.

The market sees 44 bps of easing by year end at the moment. Higher than expected figures will likely trigger a more hawkish repricing with just one rate cut becoming the base case. Conversely, lower than expected numbers should either keep the market priced for two cuts or add some probabilities for a third one.

Central bank speakers:
